speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your baby's condition, could you describe his typical feeding behavior and stool pattern in more detail? Specifically, does he seem to struggle with passing stool, and has he had any episodes of vomiting or blood in his diaper?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal tenderness and distension are concerning. Has he passed any stool or gas in the last 24 hours, and has he had any episodes of vomiting, particularly if it was green or yellow?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: He was born at term, so Hirschsprung disease remains a strong possibility. Has he passed any stool since birth, and if so, was the first stool delayed beyond the typical 48-hour window for a term infant?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: I am going to perform a digital rectal examination to check for a tight sphincter and empty rectum, which are classic signs of Hirschsprung disease. I will also request an abdominal X-ray to look for signs of bowel obstruction or dilated loops of colon. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_X-ray Findings: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of dilated bowel segments with an absence of gas in the rectum, combined with the history of feeding difficulties and abdominal distension, strongly support a diagnosis of Hirschsprung disease. To confirm the transition zone and extent of aganglionosis, I will now request a contrast enema. REQUEST TEST: Contrast_Enema

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Barium_Enema Findings: A transition zone in the distal colon, compatible with Hirschsprung disease

speaker: Doctor
text: The barium enema confirms a transition zone, which is pathognomonic for Hirschsprung disease in this clinical context. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease
